title: Stopping ventilation may not be enough in oxygen-enriched cabins
observation: In quiescent microgravity, BRE flames emulating condensed materials (e.g. PMMA, nylon) kept burning quasi-steadily in the elevated-oxygen atmospheres considered for future spacecraft, whereas comparable flames at 21 % O2 self-extinguished in a short time. PSI describes these results as preliminary.
conditions: ACME BRE (PSI-20): porous burners 25/50 mm, CH4 or C2H4, no forced flow, O2 21–40 % in the session table.
design_question: Is ventilation shutdown — an established step in fighting spacecraft fires — still a sufficient first response at 26.5–34 % O2, or must agent discharge come sooner?
limitation: Gaseous emulation of solids; per-test pressure not in the summary table; results flagged preliminary.
next_validation: Burn real cabin materials at exploration atmospheres in microgravity and partial gravity (e.g. FM2).

title: 1-g material screening is not automatically conservative
observation: Spacecraft material selection relies on NASA-STD-6001 Test 1, which ranks materials by 1-g behaviour. BASS and BASS-II were built on the hypothesis that, with adequate ventilation, materials burn as well if not better in microgravity than in normal gravity.
conditions: BASS / BASS-II (PSI-26, PSI-25): cm-scale fabric and PMMA samples, low-speed forced flow in the MSG.
design_question: Which flow speeds and flow directions must a microgravity-relevant material test include?
limitation: Specific materials and geometries; flow and O2 per test partly only in raw files for BASS.
next_validation: Extend to the materials and thicknesses of the target vehicle (SoFIE on ISS).

title: Detectors must be checked against microgravity smoke, not Earth smoke
observation: SAME was designed around the hypothesis that, without buoyant flows, smoke particles from pyrolysing materials grow larger than in 1 g; SAME and SAME-R provide quantitative data on detector sensitivity to reduced-gravity smoke.
conditions: SAME / SAME-R (PSI-102, PSI-101): Kapton, silicone, lamp wick, Pyrell, Teflon; inlet flow 0–8.1 cm/s; controlled aging times.
design_question: Which particle-size range and smoke-aging time should a spacecraft detector be qualified for?
limitation: Pyrolysis (non-flaming) smoke; particle-size results are in reports/raw files, not in the summary table.
next_validation: Test candidate detectors against SAME-like smoke at exploration atmospheres.

title: Dust can look like smoke to a particle counter
observation: DAFT showed that a modified commercial particle counter could be used in microgravity, measuring a test dust aerosol released on the ISS.
conditions: DAFT / DAFT-2 (PSI-47): 2 sessions, Arizona Road Dust in ISS nitrogen, P-Trak vs DustTrak.
design_question: On the Moon, regolith dust will enter habitats: how will detectors discriminate dust from smoke to avoid nuisance alarms?
limitation: Terrestrial test dust, not lunar regolith; feasibility test only.
next_validation: Characterise detector response to lunar-simulant dust versus SAME-type smoke.

title: Cool flames: combustion at 500–1000 K
observation: Cool diffusion flames have peak temperatures of about 500–1000 K. FLEX, CFI and CFI-G studied them on droplets and burners in microgravity.
conditions: CFI-G (PSI-159), CFI (PSI-39), FLEX (PSI-69): hydrocarbon fuels, 0.5–5 atm.
design_question: Could low-temperature reaction zones persist after visible flame extinction, and would optical or heat detectors see them?
limitation: Research fuels and configurations; relevance to cabin fires is an open question, not a finding.
next_validation: Check whether cabin-relevant fuels can sustain cool-flame chemistry in exploration atmospheres.

title: No partial-gravity combustion data yet
observation: PSI currently holds no combustion data at lunar or martian gravity. The challenge notes that microgravity and normal-gravity results can bound intermediate gravity levels, and that E-FIELD (PSI-22) mimicked partial gravity with ion-driven forces.
conditions: All PSI combustion investigations: microgravity (ISS, Cygnus) or ground.
design_question: For a Moon base, which results are bounding cases and which cannot be transferred at all?
limitation: Bounding is not interpolation: behaviour at 1/6 g may not lie between the two cases for every metric.

title: Scale matters: only SAFFIRE burned spacecraft-size samples
observation: SAFFIRE-I and -III burned ~0.4 m × 0.94 m fabric samples in uncrewed Cygnus vehicles, with O2/CO2, pressure, temperature and flame-growth measurements — the only realistic-scale fire data in PSI.
conditions: SAFFIRE-I (PSI-98) at 20 cm/s; SAFFIRE-III (PSI-100) at 30 cm/s; concurrent and opposed flow.
design_question: How do fire growth and gas-concentration changes in a sealed vehicle inform detection and response time?
limitation: Two samples per mission, one material (SIBAL).
next_validation: Additional materials at exploration atmospheres (later SAFFIRE flights).

title: More oxygen: droplet flames more often survive to burnout
observation: FLEX droplet tests in N2-only atmospheres that ended in flame extinction before burnout — Heptane: 5/17 at 21 % O2 vs 0/11 at 30–34 % O2; Methanol: 9/12 at 21 % O2 vs 2/13 at 30–34 % O2. Remaining tests ended in burnout ('completion') or droplet disruption.
conditions: FLEX (PSI-69), 274 tests, methanol and heptane droplets, O2 0.12–0.34; 103 tests near 0.7 atm (≈10.2 psia).
design_question: How much more agent (CO2, He) or O2 depletion is needed to suppress a fire at exploration-atmosphere oxygen levels than at 21 % O2?
limitation: Isolated droplets, two fuels; 'extinction' here means the flame went out before the droplet was consumed (often radiative), not the action of an extinguisher. Counts, not a model.
next_validation: Repeat at fixed droplet size and pressure; extend to solid cabin materials (BASS/SoFIE).

title: FLEX compares CO2 and helium as gaseous suppressants
observation: At 21 % O2, share of FLEX tests ending in flame extinction before burnout by atmosphere — N2 only: 14/29; CO2: 13/18; He: 7/7. FLEX varied CO2 up to 0.7 and He up to 0.45 mole fraction.
conditions: FLEX (PSI-69), methanol and heptane droplets, mostly 1 atm and 0.7 atm.
design_question: Which inert agent and which concentration should a portable or fixed extinguisher deliver in a small cabin?
limitation: Small samples per cell; droplet size and pressure also vary — use the Extract module to control for them.
next_validation: Fit extinction diameter vs agent concentration at fixed pressure; compare with FLEX-2 and models (PSI-142).

title: Microgravity and 1-g rankings of materials can disagree
observation: In SAFFIRE-II, 4 of 4 silicone samples (0.27–1.03 mm) had a burn length of about 0 in microgravity at 20 cm/s, while 2 of the 4 matching 1-g reference burns were complete. Flames did spread in microgravity over: PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric).
conditions: SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99): 5 cm-wide samples, 20 cm/s, ~21.5–22.1 % O2, Cygnus vehicle.
design_question: A 1-g screening result can be optimistic for some materials (BASS hypothesis) and pessimistic for others — which materials of a given vehicle need microgravity testing?
limitation: One test per configuration; single flow speed and near-normal O2.
next_validation: Repeat silicone at exploration-atmosphere O2 and lower flow speeds.

title: BASS-II maps solid-fuel burning down to 13.6 % O2
observation: BASS-II ran 129 tests with initial O2 between 13.6 and 22.2 % vol, mostly on PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric), Nomex. Flow annotations record extinction in 15 tests, blow-off in 3 and no ignition in 1.
conditions: BASS-II (PSI-25), MSG flow duct, flow settings up to ~49 (display units, assumed cm/s).
design_question: What O2 and flow combinations define the flammability boundary of common cabin plastics in microgravity?
limitation: Outcome annotations are free text; flow units to be confirmed in the BASS-II documentation; flame-spread rates are in the raw video data.
next_validation: Extract spread rates from the raw videos for a subset (e.g. 2 cm PMMA films).
